plan.disposition: Phase Matrix: Mini-Plan is FEATURE-only at small complexity; this is a BUG intent, no risk flags, small (classify_complexity.py: small, confidence 0.6, no risk flags) - skipped per the matrix, not an operator decline.

findings.finding: Unreachable-but-defensive guard comment was imprecise about why it's unreachable.
synthesize_ancestor silently picked the alphabetically-first parent name if a future catalog change ever gave a synthesized ancestor multiple valid non-None parents.
Empty-children precondition for synthesize_ancestor was implicit, not documented.

Claim under doubt: The synthesized ancestor's envelope (earliest start, latest end) honestly represents when that phase happened. — Two children sharing the same missing declared parent name but temporally disjoint (e.g. a phase re-entered hours apart in one long/resumed session) merge into ONE derived span whose duration spans the whole gap, not just real activity - misleading an operator reading the throughput report. Not exploitable (measurement-only, never gates a verdict) and not observed in either real production run inspected (both were tight single-episode clusters). Documented as a known limitation in iterate-timings.md rather than engineered around, since splitting into disjoint clusters would exceed the operator's literal 'envelope: earliest start, latest end' spec, and the existing exclusive_ms figure already surfaces the gap as elevated uncovered time.
findings.suggestion: documented as known limitation; not fixed

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Round-based resolution always converges to the correct tree, not just some tree. — Two orphan groups resolved in the SAME round synthesize independently, from only their own children - if one group's synthesized ancestor is itself nested and needs to be contained by an ancestor a DIFFERENT group synthesizes in the same round, the narrower one wins and a later-round widening never happens. Only reachable today via the delivery chain (ci_wait -> delivery_wait -> delivery, delivery's other declarer being post_ci_remediation) and only if deliver_pr.py's own real self-recorded delivery/delivery_wait spans are both silently absent - not confirmed reachable via the real CLI path, which always records them together. Falls back to rejection (pre-fix behavior), not data corruption. Documented as a known limitation with a code comment and in iterate-timings.md.
findings.suggestion: documented as known limitation; not fixed

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: _SOURCE_RANK guarantees a real record always outranks a derived one, per the operator's explicit 'an agent-emitted parent, when present, must still win over the derived one' requirement. — The original placeholder ordering was producer=0, derived=1, agent=2 - derived explicitly ranked ABOVE agent. A new direct test against _select_top_level/run_stat (bypassing _attach_parents, which happens to make this unreachable via the normal synthesis path today) proved this was a live, testable violation of the stated guarantee, not dead code.
findings.suggestion: fixed - _SOURCE_RANK reordered to producer=0, agent=1, derived=2; new test test_real_top_level_span_outranks_a_derived_one_of_the_same_name pins the guarantee directly, independent of _attach_parents.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: A derived span's outcome/labeling gives an operator enough signal to judge its trustworthiness. — A merged multi-episode derived span still reports outcome='completed', which reads as confident, with only the render layer's *(derived)* tag as the sole distinguishing signal.
findings.suggestion: no change needed - subsumed by the HIGH finding's documented limitation; the existing *(derived)* tag is the intended signal.

external_code.disposition: Phase Matrix: External LLM Review is 'skip' at small complexity (Advisory in Override Classes) - not mandatory below medium; the internal review cascade (spec/code/doubt) ran instead and found and fixed real issues.
